variants.name: Routine life, low institutional trust
variants.text: Simulated respondents find daily life routine yet pretty happy, and keep social contact modest, mostly a few evenings a month or year. They hold middling-to-low trust in institutions and in other people, and tend to be wary of politics without being disengaged. Their views on family and work are mixed, and they are cautious rather than enthusiastic about technology and AI.

variants.name: Stable finances, skeptical of democracy
variants.text: These respondents describe their finances as stable, with income placed around average or below and little recent change. They are dissatisfied with how democracy works while still paying close attention to political news and checking claims online. Their outlook on the economy and tax burden runs negative, and their attitudes toward technology and robots vary from concerned to neutral.

variants.name: Cautious, ambivalent, middling outlook
variants.text: Answers cluster around the midpoint on many scales: moderate trust, neither clearly positive nor negative views of the economy, and mixed agreement on statements about work and family. Respondents report being pretty happy but not excited by life, and their social time is infrequent. Their attitudes toward AI and automation are split, with reservations that shift case by case rather than a single firm stance.

variants.name: Distrustful, disengaged, content with routine
variants.text: Respondents combine low interpersonal trust with near-total disengagement from politics, yet still report being fairly satisfied with democracy and pretty happy overall. They rarely verify information they encounter online and seldom socialize beyond close family or nearby circles. Their life outlook feels exciting and personally settled rather than anxious, even though they distrust people broadly, and they hold the institutions around them in very low regard while keeping a steady, unchanged financial footing.

variants.name: Trusting, politically engaged, financially strained
variants.text: Respondents combine high general trust in people with very high political interest and active fact-checking of online political information, while reporting a worsening household financial situation and a working-class self-identification. They feel strongly that taxes are too low and see the economy as very good, despite their own financial stress. Institutional trust is polarized: they either give complete trust or none at all, with little middle ground.

variants.name: Tech-anxious, dull-life skeptics
variants.text: These respondents pair a sense of routine and dullness in daily life with strong unease about automation and artificial intelligence, expressing high worry and discomfort at machines performing human tasks. They agree that technology is a broadly positive force yet still feel it threatens people. Their social life is narrow and infrequent, leaning toward occasional outings with non-neighbourhood friends and rare family gatherings, and they hold traditional views on work and family roles.

variants.name: Distrustful, politically engaged, financially strained
variants.text: Respondents combine high political interest with deep distrust of institutions and other people, and strong dissatisfaction with democracy and their own finances. They feel economically pressed but still describe their lives as exciting and their overall happiness as fairly good. Their social lives are thin, with little regular time spent with friends or relatives, and their views on technology and science funding stay mixed or cautious.

variants.name: Isolated, low-trust, anxious-about-money
variants.text: This pattern centers on withdrawal from social ties and low confidence in strangers and institutions, combined with the sense of falling behind economically. Respondents see their family income as well below typical levels and feel the economy is doing badly, though they stay satisfied with their personal happiness. Attitudes toward automation swing between strong enthusiasm for technology and discomfort with delegating tasks to machines.

variants.name: Content with routine and family
variants.text: Respondents who describe their lives as very happy but routine, with strong and frequent ties to relatives and fewer outings with outside friends. Their financial picture is stable and improving, and they see their own standing as middle-of-the-road, so contentment and ordinary rhythms reinforce one another.

variants.name: Skeptical of technology and science
variants.text: Respondents who are cautious about robots and artificial intelligence, uncomfortable with machines taking over human tasks, and feel science receives too much funding. Their neutral stance on technology in general pairs with strong discomfort toward automation, suggesting a consistent wariness of technological change.
